doc.title: Jay McShann interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 12, 1996

title: Meeting Count Basie through Walter Bales's three-piano sessions
summary: He arrived in Kansas City after Basie left; pianist Walter Bales rented rooms with two or three pianos where he met Basie.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: Were you and Count Basie in Kansas City about the same time?
Yes. Well I came in right after Basie left and went east.
You and the count were kind of compatriots in the same kind of music.

Yes, well see there was a white fellow there, he played piano too. Named Walter Bales in Kansas City. And Walter liked to play for himself. And he’d listen to me, and he’d get together and he’d rent a piano room and he’d rent it and he and Basie, they’d get together, and he’d rent the room for two pianos in it. And then after I came to Kansas City, he would get three pianos, because Basie would be coming through on a tour, he’d say, “Bill will be in town” so he says, “get ready, I’m going to rent three pianos in the room down there at the Jenkins.” So we’d go down there and we’d have three pianos. And we’d just have a ball, the three of us. And that’s how I met Basie. And he and Walter © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -9-
Bales, they were very good friends. They’d been friends, Basie used to come out to his house and play you know, play the piano you know.
